title: KUJO — Trust at the speed of AI.
description: Kujo investor briefing: verified engineering, a proposed team evidence service, commercial validation and financing scenarios.

slides.title:
Trust at the
speed of AI.
slides.copy: Kujo makes agent-driven engineering work inspectable, repeatable and accountable across existing workflows.

slides.title: Software production is outpacing verification.
slides.copy: Agents can report completion. Teams still need a reviewable chain from requested work to release decision.

features.title: The claim
features.copy: “Tests passed. Ready to merge.” An illustrative agent statement.

features.title: The evidence
features.copy: Command, exit code, changed revision, environment and retained failure output.

features.title: The gap
features.copy: Useful logs already exist. Connecting them across tools and review boundaries remains work.

slides.title: Agents now work across the repository.
slides.copy: GitHub documents agents that plan changes, edit code and review pull requests. More delegated work makes the execution record part of the review.
slides.note: C01 · current GitHub documentation; category context, not Kujo demand

features.title: More scope
features.copy: Agents move from suggestions to repository tasks.

features.title: More handoffs
features.copy: The reviewer needs the revision, executed checks and retained failures.

features.title: Why now
features.copy: Existing platforms establish the workflow; Kujo proposes a portable evidence layer.

slides.title: A passing summary can hide a failed checkout.
slides.copy: A coupon changes a $50 cart to $50.99 instead of $45. The reviewer needs the failing test, exact change and unchanged checks.
slides.note: D01 · controlled checkout regression; buyer cost remains a hypothesis

features.title: Reconstruct
features.copy: Find the task, revision, environment and actual command result.

features.title: Correct
features.copy: Fix shipping eligibility without weakening the test.

features.title: Review
features.copy: Compare before and after evidence. Measure buyer investigation time in pilots.

slides.title: Build with clarity. Operate with control.
slides.copy: The language is the long-term foundation. Existing tools offer an earlier route into engineering workflows.

features.title: Clarity
features.copy: Kujo language / Spec / Eval: explicit intent and testable outcomes.

features.title: Context
features.copy: MCP / CaseFile / RunLedger: useful inputs, debugging evidence and run records.

features.title: Control
features.copy: Dispatch / Workcell / ShipCheck: orchestration, bounded execution and release checks.

slides.title: Accountability spans the whole task.
slides.copy: Each component owns a specific responsibility. A reviewable workflow composes their artifacts explicitly.
slides.note: Composition map; not automatic end-to-end enforcement

features.title: Instruction → Context
features.copy: Spec / PackWrite → MCP and repository context

features.title: Execution → Evaluation
features.copy: Dispatch / Workcell → Eval result artifacts

features.title: Evidence → Review → Release
features.copy: CaseFile / RunLedger → reviewer → ShipCheck gate

slides.title: A working foundation precedes this raise.
slides.copy: The language, execution tools and integration adapters are inspectable in public source.
slides.note: T01–T14, I01–I04 · documented scope; demo tools rerun locally

features.title: Language and VM
features.copy: Kujo v1.9.0 release documentation; compiler and VM source pinned for diligence.

features.title: Workflow tooling
features.copy: CaseFile captures commands. Eval runs checks. Workcell documents bounded execution.

features.title: Existing entry points
features.copy: Command Code, Hermes, OpenCode and Pi adapters have documented releases and scoped verification.

slides.title: Keep the failure. Verify the correction.
slides.copy: A reproducible checkout regression: a coupon must preserve free shipping. The original tests fail, a one-line correction passes them.
slides.note: D01 · controlled fixture; driver applies correction, no autonomous-repair claim

features.title: Before
features.copy: Python test fails: 5099 cents returned instead of 4500.

features.title: Correction
features.copy: Check the original subtotal for shipping eligibility.

features.title: After
features.copy: The same three tests pass. CaseFile retains both runs; Eval reruns the gate.

slides.title: Adopt the ecosystem before the language.
slides.copy: Keep application code in its existing language. Introduce accountability at the workflow boundary.
slides.note: T02–T04, T08 · tools have their own runtime dependencies

features.title: Today: wrap the task
features.copy: Use CaseFile for command evidence and Eval for explicit repository checks.

features.title: Then: control execution
features.copy: Adopt Dispatch or Workcell after validating the target environment and runtime pins.

features.title: Over time: go deeper
features.copy: Choose Kujo for new agent tooling where native language integration adds value.

slides.title: Start with the platform engineering lead.
slides.copy: Initial buyer hypothesis: a team operating coding agents across repositories and reconstructing failures during review.
slides.note: Buyer, demand and willingness to pay remain unvalidated

features.title: Purchase trigger
features.copy: An agent regression crosses a review boundary and the team must reconstruct what ran.

features.title: What we know
features.copy: Local evidence tools work; integration adapters and a public catalog are available.

features.title: What we are testing
features.copy: Whether shared evidence saves review effort and earns a recurring team budget.

slides.title: Open tools today. A team service to validate.
slides.copy: Primary paid wedge: shared agent-run evidence and review for engineering teams. Application code stays in its existing language.

features.title: Available now · open source

features.title: Planned · team service

features.title: Planned · enterprise
features.copy: Separate $24K/year hypothesis for deployment, policy and support. Excluded from the base case.

slides.title: A clear path from team adoption to recurring revenue.
slides.copy: One team subscription at $500 per month. Scale revenue through retained teams and repeatable adoption.
slides.note: Illustrative ARR · Paying teams × $500 × 12 · Enterprise revenue excluded

slides.title: Portable evidence across existing workflows.
slides.copy: GitHub integrates agents and review. LangGraph persists workflow state. Kujo composes local execution artifacts with explicit evaluation.
slides.note: C01–C04 · documentation comparison; no measured superiority

features.title: Demonstrated
features.copy: Before/after command bundles, unchanged checks and an inspectable patch in the checkout demo.

features.title: Interoperable
features.copy: Existing application languages and documented host adapters; exports stay reviewable outside a chat.

features.title: To earn
features.copy: A reliable shared service, useful integrations and retained buyer usage. Competitive parity is not a benchmark.

slides.title: Turn a first evidence run into a retained team.
slides.copy: Integration-led distribution: one useful repository workflow, then a buyer conversation about shared review.
slides.note: Proposed 30/60/90-day plan; no completed interviews or pilots claimed

features.title: Discover → activate
features.copy: Docs, MCP catalog and host adapters → first captured failure and passing rerun.

features.title: Validate → pilot

features.title: Convert → retain
features.copy: Offer a scoped paid pilot after readiness checks; measure weekly use, review time and renewal.

slides.title: Public engineering and distribution are visible.
